DS_7a3acef4f3.displayName: Aligned genomic sequence reads - 12 strains of hybrids
DS_7a3acef4f3.description:
Whole genome resequencing data from 12 strains of hybrids of Leishmania infantum were analyzed for single nucleotide polymorphisms and copy number variation using L. infantum JPCM5 as a reference.

SNP analysis
Reads are aligned to the reference genome using Bowtie 2 and realigned around indels using GATK. SNPs, indels and concensus sequence are generated with VARSCAN and stored in the database.

CNV analysis
The median read depth is set to the organism's ploidy and each chromosome's median read depth is normalized to this value. Contigs that are not assigned to chromosome are excluded from this analysis. Gene copy number is similarly calculated using a normalized read depth for each gene. To compare the number of genes in the resequenced genome to the reference genome, genes are grouped into clusters that are inferred to have originated by tandem duplication.
Isolate information
Whole genome analysis of population diversity from vector-derived strains. 12 strains of L. infantum that were isolated from a focus of cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) in the Cukurova province of southeast Turkey as part of a large-scale survey of both vectors and patients in this region. There are no visceral leishmaniasis (VL) cases reported in this region. 11 of these 12 CUK strains were isolated from sand flies (specifically Phlebotomus tobbi), while only a single isolate was of human origin.

DS_3b1640237f.displayName: Host specific transcriptional response in Sclerotinia sclerotiorum (SE)
DS_3b1640237f.description:
General Description: The host range of parasites is an important factor in assessing the dynamics of disease epidemics. The evolution of pathogens to accommodate new hosts may lead to host range expansion, a process the molecular bases of which are largely enigmatic. The fungus S. sclerotiorum parasitizes more than 400 plant species from diverse eudicot families.

Methodology used: Periphery and center of S. sclerotiorum disease lesions on A. thaliana (Ath), S. lycopersicum (Sly), H. annuus (Han). EDAUD_Y9I5UEJtdp0JU.displayName: T. gondii genotyping in Sea Otters & Carnivores
EDAUD_Y9I5UEJtdp0JU.shortDisplayName: T. gondii genotyping in Sea Otters & Carnivores
EDAUD_Y9I5UEJtdp0JU.description:
This dataset comprises 218 records from studies of Toxoplasma gondii infection in California coastal wildlife, combining sea otter (Enhydra lutris nereis) and terrestrial carnivore samples collected primarily along the central California coast. Sea otter records include multi-locus sequence typing (MLST) genotype data across six loci (B1, L358, PK1, SAG1, BTUB, GRA6), stranding location, year, and cause of death. Carnivore records span four species groups — bobcats, canids, feral cats, and mountain lions — and include serological data (antibody titers and seropositivity indicators for T. gondii, Sarcocystis neurona, and Neospora caninum), retroviral screening results (FIV and FeLV), B1 gene genotyping, and predominant habitat classification.

Together, the two components of this dataset support investigation of T. gondii transmission dynamics at the wildlife-domestic animal interface in coastal California. The shared genotyping variables (B1 genotype, ToxoDB genotype) and geographic coordinates (latitude/longitude) allow direct comparison of parasite strains circulating in marine and terrestrial hosts, enabling assessment of whether land-based carnivores — particularly those in urban and agricultural habitats — serve as a source of T. gondii strains reaching the nearshore marine environment and infecting sea otters.

DS_e506a29817.displayName: SNP calls on WGS of six clinical isolates of A. lentulus
DS_e506a29817.description:

As a result of their near identical morphological characteristics, most of these cryptic species have only recently been described. For example, Aspergillus lentulus was first described in 2005 in a case of human aspergillosis.

Methodology used: Sequencing technology: PacBio RSII

DS_bf29d66362.displayName: Sporulation in two stains of E maxima (APU-1, APU02)
DS_bf29d66362.description: Two strains of Eimeria maxima (APU-1 and APU-2) differ in pathogenesis in vivo: the APU-1 strain is consistently more pathogenic than the APU-2 strain. This study compares the strains' transcriptomes to delineate shared and distinct extrinsic development in two strains of Eimeria exhibiting contrasting virulence in their natural host. RNA sequencing we performed on biological triplicate of each strain at 0, 6, 12, 18, 24, 36, and 48 hours during sporulation.

DS_ecf7f76ba2.description:

DS_79549674a3.displayName: Global transcriptional response to various environmental stresses, alone and in combinations
DS_79549674a3.description:
General Description: A study was carried out to characterise the global transcriptional response of Candida albicans to various environmental stresses, alone and in combinations.

Methodology used: Candida albicans (strain CAI4-CIp10) was grown in YPD-T (Tris buffered YPD: 2% w/v glucose, 2% w/v mycological peptone, 1% w/v yeast extract, 100 mM Tris.HCl, pH 7.4) to mid-exponential phase Cultures were split and exposed to stresses in fresh medium at an OD600 of 0.2. Biological triplicate cultures were processed After 10 min cells were flash frozen in liquid nitrogen and RNA was extracted using Qiazol (phenol/chloroform method). An unstressed sample (timepoint 0 min) was used as control. RNA was DNase treated using Ambion Turbo DNAfree kit before being sent to GenePool. Libraries were prepared using standard Illumina RNAseq library preparation kit.

DS_dd73524c7e.displayName: SNP calls of WGS of Parastagonospora nodorum isolates
DS_dd73524c7e.description:
General Description: Fragments of mycelium from 4-day-old colonies growing on PDA media were transferred to 50 ml Potato Dextrose Broth (PDB) media and cultured for 4–6 days at 24 °C while shaking at 120 rpm. The resulting mycelial colonies were filtered through sterile cheesecloth and lyophilized for 72 h. Dried fungal material was used for DNA extraction with the DNeasy Plant Mini Kit (Qiagen) following the manufacturer’s standard protocol. We sequenced the genomes for all 159 isolates included in this study.  

Methodology used: The sequencing was performed on an Illumina HiSeq 2500 platform producing paired-end reads of 150 bp. Preparation of sequencing libraries and sequencing was performed at the Functional Genomics Center in Zurich.

DS_c788cd2be6.displayName: Transcriptomes of Phytophthora infestans at mycelium stage
DS_c788cd2be6.description:
General Description: The potato late blight pathogen Phytophthora infestans has both an asexual and a sexual mode of reproduction. In Scandinavia, the pathogen is reproducing sexually on a regular basis, whereas clonal lineages dominate in other geographical regions. This study aimed at elucidating events or key genes underlying this difference in sexual behavior. Eight P. infestans strains from potato were included in the mating experiments; four from Sweden (Sw1_A1, Sw2_A2, Sw3_A1, and Sw4_A2), two from the Netherlands (F80029_A1 and IPO82001_A2) and two from the United Kingdom (Pink 6_A1 and Blue 13/3928A_A2).

Methodology used: Isolates with A1 and A2 mating types from Sweden, the Netherlands and the UK, were used for this purpose because mating frequencies are known to differ among European countries. RNA was prepared from the “mating-zone” between the 4 Swedish, 1 Dutch and 1 British pairs. In total 14 samples were analyzed. The mating samples (m3-m10) contained 3 biological replicates, while the control samples (s1-s8) contained 2 biological replicates. Illumina HiSeq 2500 (Phytophthora infestans).

DS_29465e6433.displayName: SNP calls on WGS of Coccidioides isolates from the Western Hemisphere
DS_29465e6433.description: Coccidioides immitis and C. posadasii are pathogenic environmental fungi causing coccidioidomycosis primarily in the desert Southwest of the United States, with scattered endemic foci throughout the Western Hemisphere. The complexities of their recombining genomes has, until recently, limited the development of tools for molecular epidemiology and phylogeographic analysis at both the regional and local levels. Here we perform whole genome sequence analyses of 64 new and 28 previously published genomes to ascertain the population structure of Coccidioides, particularly within local subpopulations of C. posadasii. The results provide evidence of substantial population structure in C. posadasii and demonstrate presence of distinct geographic clades in Central and Southern Arizona as well as dispersed populations in Texas, Mexico and South and Central America. Although a smaller number of C. immitis strains were included in the analyses, some evidence of phylogeographic structure was detected in this species as well. Specifically, newly identified clinical and environmental strains from Washington State formed a distinct well-supported clade on C. immitis genomic phylogeny. Phylogenetic analyses indicated that C. posadasii is the most ancient of the two species, and Southern Arizona contains the most diverse subpopulations. A model for distribution of C. posadasii out of the Southern Arizona region is proposed.

DS_43f8972148.displayName: Individual Hawaiian mosquitoes response to the avian malaria parasite Plasmodium relictum
DS_43f8972148.shortDisplayName: Individual Hawaiian mosquitoes response to P. relictum
DS_43f8972148.description:
Offspring of wild-collected Hawaiian Cx. quinquefasciatus were fed on a domestic canary infected with a fresh isolate of Plasmodium relictum GRW4 from a wild-caught Hawaiian honeycreeper (Hawaiʻi ‘amakihi, Chlorodrepanis virens). Control mosquitoes were fed on an uninfected canary (Serinus canaria). Transcriptomes of five infected and three uninfected individual mosquitoes were sequenced at each of the three stages of the parasite life cycle. All 48 libraries were pooled in an equimolar fashion and submitted to Genewiz (South Plainfield, NJ, USA) for paired-end sequencing (2 × 150 bp) in one lane of Illumina HiSeq 2500 (BioProject: PRJNA779986).


Samples:
  • 24 h post feeding (hpf) during ookinete invasion
  • days post feeding (dpf) when oocysts are developing
  • 10 dpf when sporozoites are released and invade the salivary glands

Our study is the first to analyze non-Anopheles transcriptome responses to Plasmodium, and will allow comparisons between mammalian and avian malaria systems.

DS_1b46735880.description: The malaria mosquito Anopheles gambiae has a high preference for human hosts, a characteristic that contributes greatly to its capacity for transmitting human malaria. A sibling species, An. quadriannulatus, has a quite different host preference and feeds mostly on bovids. For this reason it does not contribute to human malaria transmission. Host seeking in mosquitoes is modulated by the olfactory system, which is primarily housed in the antennae and maxillary palps. Therefore, the detection of differing host odors by sibling species may be reflected in the expression level of the olfactory genes involved. Accordingly, we compared the transcriptomes of the antennae and maxillary palps of An. gambiae and An. quadriannulatus.

DS_eed7a85cbd.displayName: Liver stage hypnozoite vs schizont transcriptomes (primary culture)
DS_eed7a85cbd.description:
Transcriptomics of hypnozoite and sporozoite stages from Plasmodium cynomolgi
Six to seven days after P. cynomolgi strain M sporozoite infection of primary simian hepatocytes, FACS-purified hepatocytes containing hypnozoites and liver schizonts were prepared for high-throughput RNA-Seq. The dataset contains three independent schizont samples and four independent hypnozoite samples.

DS_79b90cb45e.description:
Sex determination evolves rapidly, often because of turnover of the genes at the top of the pathway. The house fly, Musca domestica, has a multifactorial sex determination system, allowing us to identify the selective forces responsible for the evolutionary turnover of sex determination in action. There is a male determining factor, M, on the Y chromosome (Y^M), which is probably the ancestral state. An M factor on the third chromosome (III^M) has reached high frequencies in multiple populations across the world, but the evolutionary forces responsible for the invasion of III^M are not resolved. To test if the III^M chromosome invaded because of sex-specific selection pressures, we used mRNA-Seq to determine if isogenic males that differ only in the presence of the Y^M or III^M chromosome have different gene expression profiles.

Overall design: 3 replicates of testes and male heads from a Y^M and a III^M strain, and one sample of head and ovary from each of the strains.

Strain Info: We compared gene expression between two nearly isogenic house fly strains that differ only in the chromosome carrying M. The first, Cornell susceptible (CS), is an inbred, lab adapted strain with XX males that are heterozygous for a IIIM chromosome and a standard third chromosome that lacks an M factor (X/X; IIIM/IIICS) . CS females are XX and homozygous for the standard third chromosome (X/X; IIICS/IIICS). We created a strain with YM males that has the X chromosome and all standard autosomes from the CS strain. To do so, we used a backcrossing approach to move the Y chromosome from the genome strain (aabys) onto the CS background, creating the strain CS-aabys-Y (CSaY). CSaY males are XY and homozygous for the standard CS third chromosome (X/Y; IIICS/IIICS). The aabys strain has a recessive phenotypic marker on each of the five autosomes.

DS_0fdca599cd.displayName: Treatment-time to reinfection cohort from Kisumu area, Kenya collected in 2003
DS_0fdca599cd.description:
Protein microarrays were probed with plasma from residents of a community in Kenya monitored for 12 weeks for reinfection and symptomatic malaria after administration of antimalarial drugs. P. falciparum proteins recognized by Abs from 88 children, aged 1-14 years, and 86 adults, aged 18 years, measured at the beginning of the observation period, were ranked by Ab signal intensity.

These data are the result of a collaborative effort in multiple International Centers of Excellence in Malaria Research (ICEMRs) to develop tests using malaria-specific antibody responses as biosignatures of transmission and immunity.

DS_64fa10a3d2.displayName: Cryptosporidium hominis genetic diversity in isolates from Bangladesh (C parvum aligned)
DS_64fa10a3d2.description: Genome sequencing of Cryptosporidium hominis from infants in slum dwelling from Dhaka Bangladesh. Cryptosporidium oocysts were purified directly from stool samples of 2 grams of semi-solid stool or approximately 2 mL of liquid stool material using the protocol of Hadfield et al. In 32 samples the sequences were both derived from C. hominis and had >80% genome coverage of 10X. Fifteen of these were diarrheal isolates and seventeen were isolated from subclinical infections as defined by Steiner et al.

DS_113b047941.description: Comparison of the transcriptional profile of specific-tissues of the Aedes aegypti mosquitoes following a not-infectious or a DENV2-Jam1409 infectious blood-meal.

DS_42159a7b38.displayName: SNP calls on WGS of six F. graminearum strains collected from wheat fields in France
DS_42159a7b38.description:
General Description: Six strains of Fusarium graminearum sensu stricto were isolated from wheat plants cultivated in several French regions (Cher, Meuse, Eure, Gers, and Seine Maritime) between 2001 and 2002. These strains exhibit various trends of pathogenicity and quantitative profiles of DON/15-ADON production that are representative of the genotypic and phenotypic diversity observed within a larger French collection of isolates (for more information refer to Table 5).

Methodology used: Illumina HiSeq 2000

DS_b15b7077f9.description:
General Description: The paired-end dual RNA-seq was performed between Cryptococcus neoformans H99 and the rodent (Mus musculus) and primate host (Macaca fascicularis) using three biological replicates.

Methodology used: Expression profiling by high throughput sequencing - Illumina NextSeq 500.

DS_ed416e9e01.description: Mosquitoes that emerged over a 24-h period were either directly collected as 0- to 1-day-old adults, or isolated for later collection time points of 1- to 2-day-old and 2- to 3-day-old adults. For each time point, five mosquitoes were homogenized in 300 µl RNA lysis buffer (Zymo Research) and stored at −80 °C until RNA isolation. For RNA isolation, equal volumes of homogenate from each time point were combined to represent 0- to 3-day-old mosquitoes. These steps were performed in biological triplicates for males and virgin nonblood-feed females of both An. stephensi and Ae. aegypti. Illumina paired-end libraries for the resulting samples were prepared using the manufacturer’s specific protocol. The libraries were then sequenced using Illumina HiSeq.

DS_16686ed2dc.displayName: Malpighian tubules transcriptome, blood vs sugar fed
DS_16686ed2dc.shortDisplayName: Malpighian tubules, blood vs sugar fed
DS_16686ed2dc.description:
Twelve replicates were collected for non-blood-fed mosquitoes and 3 replicates each were collected for blood-fed mosquitoes at 3h, 12h, and 24h post-blood meal.
Paired-end libraries were sequenced in one lane using Illumina HiSeq 2000 platform.

Aedes albopictus (ALBOPICTUS, MRA-804, deposited by Sandra Allan) were obtained from the Malaria Research and Reference Reagent Resource Center (MR4) as part of BEI Resources Repository, NIAID, NIH.

For a given experimental trial, 90 adult female mosquitoes were transferred from the main colony to two small containers (45 females per container) and starved for 24 h by removing their sucrose solution. After 24 h, one container of mosquitoes was provided with access to 10% sucrose for 30 min (non-blood-fed treatment, NBF) and the other was provided with access to heparinized rabbit blood (Hemostat Laboratories, Dixon, CA, USA) through a membrane feeder (Hemotek, Blackburn, UK) for 30 min. After 3 h, 12 h, or 24 h, mosquitoes were immobilized on ice for ∼15 min and the Malpighian tubules were isolated with fine forceps under Ringer solution

DS_200bf199c6.displayName: Whole genome sequencing of T. cruzi TcI isolates and clones
DS_200bf199c6.description: 34 different T. cruzi TcI isolates and clones from different geographic regions were Illumina sequenced and mapped against the assembled T. cruzi Sylvio X10/1 genome to identify SNPs.

DS_85213de859.displayName: Blood (with and without parasites) at 1, 4, or 9 days post blood meal
DS_85213de859.description:
Sand flies aged 5 to 9 days were fed blood or parasite-containing blood, resulting in four treatment groups of Phlebotomus papatasi females:
  1. blood meal only
  2. blood meal + L. major,
  3. blood meal + L. donovani and
  4. blood meal + Herpetomonas muscarum.
Leishmania and Herpetomonas muscarum promastigotes from log-phase cultures (3–4 days post inoculation) were resuspended in defibrinated and heat-inactivated rabbit blood at concentration of 1 × 106 promastigotes/ml, which corresponds to 500–1000 promastigotes per Phlebotomus papatasi female. Sand fly females (5–9 days old) were infected by feeding on the suspension through a chick-skin membrane. Engorged sand flies were maintained under the same conditions as the colony.

Flies were then left to develop an infection or digest their non-infected blood meal for 1, 4 or 9 days (actual age = 18–19 days on ninth day PBM). Across infections, flies were compared at the same time point (same age) unless flies with the same infection were being compared.

RNA was purified from whole sand flies at 1, 4 and 9 days PBM, with the aim to identify any systemic responses over and above tissue-specific signals. Each time point analyzed included 20 flies; thus, 3 (time points) × 20 sand flies were processed per treatment group. This experiment was independently repeated three times for each treatment group so that ultimately 3 (replicates) × 60 (sand flies) =180 sand flies were processed for each treatment group in all three experiments. The goal of our experiment was to determine whether there was a difference between blood meal versus infected blood meal. Therefore, the non-infected blood meal served as the control (BioProject: PRJEB35592).

DS_4362334059.displayName: Parasite transcriptome during infection in mouse brain.
DS_4362334059.description: Transcriptional profiles generated from RNA seq analysis of laser capture microdissected neurons from mice inoculated with saline (control), type II (Pru-Cre), or type III (CEP-Cre) Toxoplasma gondii parasites. Samples include Toxoplasma-injected neurons (TINs), Bystander neurons (nearby non-Toxoplasma-injected neurons), and neurons from uninfected mice (controls).

DS_a03298576e.description:

Methodology used: cDNA libraries were sequenced, with their respective biological triplicates corresponding to the paired libraries, using an Illumina HiSeq2000 sequencer, to generate 100 bp paired-end reads.

DS_4d3aadae16.description:
Host (Mus musculus) transcriptional profile of age- and sex-matched mice during very early (21 days), early (28 days), mid (3 months), and late (6 months) chronic infection.

DS_57468051b4.displayName: Genomic diversity of 56 Trypanosoma congolense field isolates from 10 African countries
DS_57468051b4.description: 56 Trypanosoma congolense isolates collected between 1971 and 2014 were maintained in OF-1 mice. Blood samples were obtained once parasitemia reached 30-60 trypanosomes/field in wet blood films at 400x magnification. To separate parasites from the blood, parasites were eluted from an anion exchanger DEAE-cellulose resin with phosphate saline glucose (PSG). DNA was extracted using the QIAamp DNA Blood Mini Kit, and next-generation sequencing libraries were made from 1 ng DNA using the Nextera XT kit. Each library underwent a MiSeq run with a 500 or 600 cycles kit. Paired-end sequence reads were mapped to the T. congolnse IL3000 reference genome.

DS_f2d320a16d.displayName: Aligned Genomic Sequence Reads - 42 global isolates from human, tick and rodent
DS_f2d320a16d.description:
The complete genomes of 42 Babesia microti isolates, including 32 human cases, two samples from ticks and four from rodents were sequenced. Geographic location of sample origins include Northeastern USA, Midwestern USA, Alaska, Russia and Japan. The 6.4 Mb genome was sequenced to a mean depth of 153-fold on Illumina HiSeq instruments using a paired-end protocol. The data were used to calculate SNPs against the B microti reference genome.

Data were used to determine single nucleotide polymorphisms against the B. microti RI reference.

DS_53f554ec6a.displayName: RMgmDB - Rodent Malaria genetically modified Parasites
DS_53f554ec6a.description: The Rodent Malaria genetically modified Parasites database is a web-based, manually curated, repository containing information on genetically modified rodent-malaria parasites generated by many labs worldwide. It contains data of 3 rodent malaria parasites: Plasmodium berghei, P. yoelii and P. chabaudi. The aim of this database is to provide the research community access to detailed information on the generation (e.g. disruption, tagging, mutation, transgene expression) and phenotype of mutant malaria parasites. The database also provides information on unpublished mutants without a clear phenotype and negative trials to modify genes.
